Your requirements make sense, and the cleanest structure is this:

How the game should work

Every draw is random.

When the user clicks Flip Card:

  1. current front card flips to the back design

  2. brief back-of-card hold

  3. new random card appears on the front

  4. card content starts in hidden-answer mode

Then the controls are:

  • Flip Card = draw a new random card

  • Reveal Answer = show Professional Approach

  • Hide Answer = hide it again

  • Reset Deck = reshuffle and clear used-card memory

  • Full Screen = for TV/projector use

Card types

We should support 2 card layouts in one system:

1. Standard text card

Uses:

  • Title

  • Scenario

  • Professional Approach

2. Picture card

Uses:

  • Title

  • Image

  • Comment / prompt below image

  • optional Professional Approach if you want reveal mode on image cards too

That gives you flexibility without making two separate games.

Recommended Google Sheet columns

Use these exact columns in row 1:

CardID
CardType
Title
Scenario
ProfessionalApproach
ImageURL
ImagePrompt
Active
Category
SortOrder

What each column means

CardID

Unique ID for the card.

Examples:

  • LU-28

  • CI-17

  • SR-05

CardType

Use one of these values:

  • text

  • image

Title

Top title on the card.

Examples:

  • POOL CLOSED

  • LEVEL UP

  • NO UPGRADE AVAILABLE

Scenario

Main scenario text for standard cards.

For image cards, this can be blank if you are using ImagePrompt instead.

ProfessionalApproach

The hidden reveal text.

For image cards, this can be:

  • filled in if you want reveal mode

  • blank if the image card is discussion-only

ImageURL

Direct image link for picture cards.

For text cards, leave blank.

ImagePrompt

The text under the image.

Example:

  • WHAT DOES THIS ENERGY COMMUNICATE?

Active

Use:

  • Y

  • N

Only Y cards get loaded.

Category

Optional, but useful later for filtering.

Examples:

  • Front Desk

  • Service Recovery

  • Upgrade

  • Guest Interaction

SortOrder

Optional.
Not important for random draw, but useful for management.

Exact sheet behavior rules

For a text card:

  • use Title

  • use Scenario

  • use ProfessionalApproach

  • ignore ImageURL

  • ignore ImagePrompt

For an image card:

  • use Title

  • use ImageURL

  • use ImagePrompt

  • optionally use ProfessionalApproach for reveal

  • Scenario can be blank

Example rows

Standard text card

CardID | CardType | Title | Scenario | ProfessionalApproach | ImageURL | ImagePrompt | Active | Category | SortOrder
LU-18 | text | POOL CLOSED | Yeah, it’s closed. | I know that’s disappointing. The pool is temporarily closed for maintenance, but I’d be happy to share alternative options nearby. |  |  | Y | Service Recovery | 1

Picture card

CardID | CardType | Title | Scenario | ProfessionalApproach | ImageURL | ImagePrompt | Active | Category | SortOrder
LU-28 | image | LEVEL UP |  | A warm greeting with confident eye contact and open posture communicates readiness and professionalism. | https://...your-image-link... | WHAT DOES THIS ENERGY COMMUNICATE? | Y | Front Desk | 2

Best layout behavior

Portrait TV

Default layout should be portrait-first:

  • large single card centered

  • big readable buttons below

  • optimized for tall screens

Projector / landscape

It should automatically scale:

  • card stays centered

  • buttons shift underneath

  • card shrinks slightly to fit

So yes, we should make it responsive, not force only portrait.

Front/back card template usage

We should use:

  • Front Card template as the visible card face

  • Back Card template for the flip transition

That way every draw feels like a real card reveal.

Sound

I agree with you: skip sound for V1 unless it is genuinely good.
A weak sound effect makes it feel cheaper, not better.

Final recommendation for V1

Build this as:

  • one-card-at-a-time experience

  • random draw only

  • no repeats until reset deck

  • reveal/hide answer

  • supports both text and image cards

  • fullscreen button

  • plain HTML for Vercel

What I’ll want from you when we build it

I’ll need:

  • the Front Card template image

  • the Back Card template image

  • the Google Sheet URL

  • confirmation whether image cards should also support Professional Approach reveal

My recommendation is: yes, support reveal on image cards too, even if some rows leave it blank. That keeps the system flexible.
